ranked_facts.concept_key: characteristic milky white layer on blood sample surface

evidence_chain.link: The quote mentions lipoprotein lipase deficiency, which is a key feature of Lipoprotein Lipase Deficiency (B1) and is associated with a milky white layer on the blood sample surface.
evidence_chain.quote: One of the best characterized of these disorders is absence of functional lipoprotein lipase (LpL) activity in which VLDL catabolism is severely impaired, in particular the lipolysis of VLDL1

evidence_chain.link: The quote mentions hyperinsulinism, which is not a key feature of Glycogen Storage Disease Type I (B2) in this context.
evidence_chain.quote: Hyperinsulinism is a medical condition characterized by inappropriately high insulin secretion compared to plasma glucose concentration, leading to a continuous stimulation of hepatic glycogen synthesis and glucose uptake by skeletal muscles and adipose tissue.

ranked_facts.why: The characteristic milky white layer on the blood sample surface is a key finding that supports Lipoprotein Lipase Deficiency (B1) and contrasts with Glycogen Storage Disease Type I (B2).
